Straight from the real FAQ pages

Frequently Asked

Are classes crowded?
Yes. St. Mark’s classes are very full. Off-peak times are quieter, but as a rule expect a full room.
Do I need to sign up in advance?
Recommended but not required. At the door it is $12 cash or $13 Venmo. Full classes cannot take drop-ins.
What if I cancel?
Cancel at least one hour before class and an automatic credit lands on your account.
What style of yoga is it?
Vinyasa drawn from the Jivamukti, Katonah and Dharma lineages.
Is it beginner friendly?
All levels welcome in any class. Basics classes run Mon–Fri at 6pm and Sat–Sun at 10am and 3pm.
Showers, lockers, changing?
No showers and no lockers. Cubby shelves in each studio keep valuables in eyesight, and there are full-length changing curtains plus a small restroom in each studio.
Is there air conditioning?
Studios 2R and 4F run AC in summer. Studio 4R does not.
Can I use my phone in class?
No, absolutely not. The one exception is on-call medical professionals and doulas, who take calls in the hallway.
How does donation pricing work?
Outdoor and select studio classes are pay what you can, by cash, Zelle to 718-626-0680, or card on the website.
What should I bring?
Your own mat for outdoor classes. Indoors, mat rental is $1 at donation-based classes.
Two real histories

How Each Room Got Here

Since 1885 / revived 2021

St. Mark’s Yoga

The building at 12 St. Mark’s Place is landmarked and dates to 1885. Yoga began here in 1990 under Henrick Kohan’s New York Yoga Center. After he left in 2003 a rotating group of teachers kept it going, until the pandemic closed it in 2020. Arts On Site kept the building from being sold.

Matthew Lombardo chanted Om and taught the first class of St. Mark’s Yoga on July 1, 2021. The mission: restore in-person practice in New York while honouring the counter-culture rebellion built into both traditional yoga and the East Village itself.

Since 2010

Yoga Agora

Founded in Astoria in 2010 and named for the agora, the central gathering place of ancient Greece. The studio calls itself a local destination for anyone who needs a community space to move, breathe and meditate.

The belief underneath it is that connection to community plays a real role in quality of life. Fifteen years on, the door price is still $12, most of the schedule is still drop-in, and the outdoor season is still open to anyone who shows up with a mat.
